text:
alice: saw a blip in ap-southeast1 today — small-write IOPS spiked around 02:14 UTC and two batch racks failed GPU attach. Anyone watching storage?
ops-bot: ALERT ap-southeast1 small_write_iops_95pct 82% over 5m on pool-nvme-7..9 :warning:
ben: i'm oncall. quick summary from host nvme-8: write ops are tiny (~4KB) but Q depth is ~60, avg latency 10-15ms, %util ~92. Not seeing immediate SMART errors.
dave: looks like janitor + checkpoint churn again. We had a similar signature last month but different racks. Propose: temporary janitor throttle + bump eviction coalesce window to 200ms. That should let writes batch.
kira: agree. small change: reduce janitor workers 6->1 and set coalesce_ms=200 for the pool. I'll prepare the flag change. Note: coalesce_ms may increase memory footprint briefly.
bен: ran flag flip: janitor.workers=1 and pool.coalesce_ms=200 for ap-southeast1. Paused new batch scheduling into two hot racks for 10 minutes. Monitoring graphs now.
dave: within 90s 95p write_iops dropped from 16k->5k and attach errors stopped. No SMART growth on wear counters yet but i'll run a light async scan.
ops-bot: RESOLVED ap-southeast1 small_write_iops back to normal :white_check_mark:
alice: good call. Create follow-up ticket INFRA-5787: evaluate long-term janitor rewrite to coalesce deletes and avoid fsync storms; also consider per-pool eviction-backoff policies. Kira, please add runbook step for threshold = 95p small-write iops > 12k + attach_failures > 2 within 10m -> throttle janitor and increase coalesce_ms.
kira: will PR runbook and add ticket.
ben: leaving note: oncall will watch for 2h and escalate if recurrence.
